gaps.invariant_impact: ROADMAP-2.2 D4 pinned-client byte-identity gate (review_ocr.pinned); not an I–IX kernel invariant but an execution-authority admission control, adjacent to INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY (authority only from the operator's pin, not from code).
gaps.rationale: getattr(settings,'client_pin',None) becomes getattr(settings,'',None), which is always None. The whole pinned-client block (533-545) is skipped, exe falls back to PATH/client_exe at 602, and pin_sha256 is never put in kw (656) so the per-session re-check in client.py:326 is also disabled. A run whose operator pinned a specific client binary now silently runs whatever is on PATH, and a replaced/wrong/updated binary that should refuse the run before any session or request instead proceeds with no rec['client_pin'] recorded. Silent authority expansion of which binary may execute. Survived because the referenced S2 kill test passes a settings stand-in WITHOUT client_pin (getattr naturally returns None there), so it cannot distinguish 'always None'.

gaps.verify_basis: UPHOLD confirmed, severity trimmed from critical to high. Control path: L532's value directly gates three things — the pre-run RunRefused (L533->L541 via review_ocr.pinned(), a genuine sha256 byte-identity check that reads the binary and compares to the operator's pin), the exe selection at L602 (pin['exe'] vs client_exe/client_on_path PATH fallback), and pin_sha256 into kw at L656, which gates the per-session re-check at client.py:322-326. Exploit is DIRECT and test-blind: no test drives execute() with a pinned settings (test_v22_client_pin_fence.py exercises only settings.load and client.session directly; test_app_run.SETTINGS and the S2 RunRecord base both omit client_pin), so real getattr and the mutant both return None — the referenced S2 kill test cannot distinguish 'always None' from 'absent'. Concrete scenario that defeats a guarantee: an operator pins an audited client binary by {exe,sha256}; a replaced/auto-updated/wrong binary that the correct kernel refuses at L541 BEFORE any session or provider request (recording rec['client_pin'].status) instead runs silently on PATH, the per-session re-check is dead, and rec['client_pin'] is absent from RUN.json — so a run-record auditor reads it as an ordinary unpinned run, not a dropped pin. That is a real refusal-bypass + execution-authority expansion + record/provenance gap. DOWNGRADE rejected: not dead code (settings parse it, execute consumes it, client re-checks it), not dominated (confine.measure and client_identity are descriptive, not an identity gate against the operator's pin; nothing re-derives it), L541 is a control action not diagnostic. Severity is HIGH not CRITICAL because the gate is opt-in defense-in-depth (client_pin optional; default PATH lookup / 2.0.0 rule is untouched, so only runs that explicitly pinned are weakened), it is explicitly NOT a frozen I–IX kernel invariant (only D4 roadmap, adjacent to INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY), and it concerns byte identity of the operator's own client ('never build provenance') rather than the destructive kill/delete/release authority that invariant governs. The proposed kill test (mismatched pin -> RunRefused naming client_pin with no session/request started; matching pin -> rec['client_pin'].status=='PASSED', resolved exe==pin['exe'], kw carries pin_sha256) would distinguish the mutant and is the correct fix.

gaps.invariant_impact: IV Typed Ownership / confinement bound; INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY (declared containment authority may not be silently widened)
gaps.rationale: fence = getattr(settings,'client_fence',None) becomes getattr(settings,'',None), which is always None because settings has no '' attribute. So when the operator DECLARES a fence it is silently ignored: the run-scoped XDG data/state/cache branch (xdg_home) is never built, and the fence kw (OPENCODE_PERMISSION allow-list limited to the run repo + output-token ceiling, G2) is never passed to developer/reviewer sessions. The client then runs with the host's real XDG and no permission allow-list while the operator believes the declared fence is in effect — a silent authority/containment expansion that produces a false confinement guarantee. No test asserts a declared client_fence is actually applied, so it survives. (confine.measure at the confinement stage is a separate control; a run that relies on client_fence without settings.confinement is fully exposed.)
gaps.kill_test_sketch: execute() with settings.client_fence={'xdg':'run-scoped',...} set: assert out/'client-xdg'/{data,state,cache} are created and that the session kw passed to Developer/Reviewer carries 'fence' with str(repo) in its 'allow' tuple (and the declared token ceiling); i.e. the fence is non-None and applied.
gaps.verify_basis: UPHELD as a real authority/confinement expansion, downgraded one notch from critical to high. With the mutant, run.py:642 yields fence=None, so (a) xdg_home dirs (L643-647) are never built and (b) neither the run-scoped XDG env nor the fence kw (L649-655) reach any session. In client.session (client.py:332-348) the whole fence block is skipped: no OPENCODE_PERMISSION default-deny allow-list ({"*":"deny", cwd/repo:"allow"}), host's real XDG_DATA/STATE/CACHE instead of run-scoped, no output-token ceiling, and the per-session result carries no "fence" line. Net: every untrusted developer/reviewer opencode session runs with host-wide filesystem authority rather than the declared worktree+run-repo bound, while the operator's declared containment sits accepted in the record — a silent widening of declared containment authority (IV typed ownership / confinement bound). The only contradicting evidence is the ABSENCE of the per-session fence line; nothing asserts the declared fence was applied. CONTROL PATH confirmed: fence/xdg_home have this single source, no re-derivation, no dominating check. SURVIVES because tests/v2/test_v22_client_pin_fence.py exercises settings.load, client.environment and client.session directly (passing fence/xdg_home itself) and never drives run.execute's L642 glue; the proposed kill test (execute() with settings.client_fence set, assert out/client-xdg/{data,state,cache} exist and the session kw fence carries str(repo) in allow + the token ceiling) would kill it. NOT critical: client_fence is by explicit, repeated design declared-only / client-enforced / NOT-measured — no invariant in invariants/registry.py backs it, there is no measured gate, and the record states "NOT measured". The hard, MEASURED confinement (settings.confinement/bwrap, the III.confinement-from-env mechanism) is a separate path untouched by this mutant, and there is no forged positive claim, no false delivery PASS/VERIFIED, and no digest/provenance forgery — the drop is a silent omission, auditable only by noticing a missing per-session line. Serious authority expansion for no-bwrap configs, below the measured-guarantee-forgery bar → high.

gaps.invariant_impact: none of I-IX directly; ROADMAP-2.2 D4 client-binary pin (provenance of the executed client, in the spirit of VI Immutable Provenance)
gaps.rationale: Entry 8 is the pin_sha256 spread `**({'pin_sha256': client_pin['sha256']} if client_pin is not None else {})`. Dropping it stops execute from handing the pin to the sessions, so client.session (client.py:322-326) skips the moment-of-use sha256 re-check. The pre-run identity check (run.py:533-545) still verifies the pin once, but the per-session re-check that closes the TOCTOU window is gone: a client binary replaced between the pre-run check and a session's exec runs unverified, while rec['client_pin'].status still reads PASSED and the session record loses 'pinned_sha256'. Provenance of the executed client is weakened silently; exploitation needs an active swap in a narrow window, so high rather than critical.
gaps.kill_test_sketch: Run execute with a settings.client_pin set and assert the kw handed to the sessions contains pin_sha256 == client_pin['sha256']; stronger: swap the binary after the pre-run check and assert the session raises SessionRefused('client_pin at the moment of use').
gaps.verify_basis: UPHOLD stands. kw entry 8 is the sole wiring that feeds pin_sha256 from execute into ad.Developer(kw)/ad.Reviewer(rkw) and onward to every client.session(**self.kw). Dropping it makes client.session receive the default pin_sha256=None, so the moment-of-use re-check (client.py:322-326, `if pin_sha256 is not None: pinned(exe,...) -> raise SessionRefused`) is silently skipped and the record field pinned_sha256 (client.py:374) is absent. Concrete scenario: operator sets settings.client_pin={exe,sha256}; execute's pre-run check (run.py:533-545) hashes the binary, passes, and records rec[client_pin].status=PASSED before any session/provider request; during the clone+preflight window (real wall-clock, real network I/O) the binary at exe is replaced (opencode auto-update / co-tenant overwrite / race). Shipped: each session re-hashes at use and raises SessionRefused('client_pin at the moment of use'), swapped bytes never run. Mutant: sessions launch the swapped, unverified binary as the developer/reviewer client, no refusal, pinned_sha256 omitted, while RUN.json still attests client_pin:PASSED — a false provenance attestation of the executed client and authority handed to unpinned bytes. DOWNGRADE fails: the value is observed (drives a hard refusal guard and a record field), not dominated (the pre-run check covers only the before-anything verification and cannot cover the strictly-later per-session re-check that closes the swap window), not re-derived (this one kw entry is the only feed; its loss yields None and skips the guard), not pure diagnostic (SessionRefused is a live control-flow guard). confirmed_control_path=true: kw -> Developer/Reviewer -> client.session on every session of a pinned run. confirmed_exploit=direct: the mutated line is itself the wiring that arms the moment-of-use guard; removing it directly lets a swapped binary execute and yields the false PASSED attestation in a single hop (the binary swap is the external precondition the guard exists to defend, not an additional defect). HIGH not CRITICAL: no armed invariant I-IX is breached (VI Immutable Provenance's registered mechanisms — full-sha, revision-in-runspec, journal-append-only, record-digest, semantic-hash, frozen-artefacts — do not include the client-pin re-check; D4 is ROADMAP-2.2 hardening in the spirit of VI), and there is no unconditional false PASS: a benign no-swap run differs only by the missing pinned_sha256 evidence field, so the guarantee defeat is gated on an active binary swap inside the pre-run-to-exec window. Real gap confirmed: tests/v2/test_v22_client_pin_fence.py::_run exercises the re-check by calling client.session directly with explicit pin_sha256, bypassing the mutated line, and no test drives execute with client_pin set to assert the kw/session carries pin_sha256; the first-pass kill test (drive execute with client_pin and assert the session kw/record carries pin_sha256==client_pin[sha256]; stronger: swap the binary after the pre-run check and assert SessionRefused) is valid and distinguishes the mutant.

gaps.invariant_impact: none — ROADMAP-2.2 D4 client-pin moment-of-use re-check (binary provenance); not a registered kernel invariant
gaps.rationale: The shipped line is `**({'pin_sha256': client_pin['sha256']} if client_pin is not None else {})`. Dropping the entry means pin_sha256 never reaches the session, so client.session's moment-of-use re-check (client.py:322-326, `pinned(exe, pin_sha256)`) is silently skipped. The pre-run check (run.py ~536) still runs before anything starts, but this is the sole defense against a TOCTOU swap of the pinned client binary BETWEEN the pre-run check and the session's actual exec: a replaced binary would be used for the paid provider work undetected, so the run's recorded client provenance would be false. Silent (the session still reports started; only the 'pinned_sha256' field in its result disappears). High: a silent provenance/identity gap with a direct forgery path, mitigated only by the one-time pre-run check. No test asserts a pinned run propagates pin_sha256 into the session so the re-check actually fires.
gaps.kill_test_sketch: With settings.client_pin set, assert kw['pin_sha256']==client_pin['sha256'] (present under that exact key) so client.session performs pinned() at the moment of use; optionally assert a mid-run binary swap raises SessionRefused.
gaps.verify_basis: UPHELD (hot rating stands at high; downgrade failed). Concrete scenario: an operator opts into D4 client_pin on a paid run. run.execute does the one-time pre-run byte check (run.py:536, passes) and resolves exe from client_pin["exe"] (run.py:602); client_identity hashes the bytes once at runspec time (run.py:309/626). With the mutant, kw no longer carries pin_sha256, so both adapters' client.session(**self.kw) calls (adapters.py:87, :181) run with pin_sha256=None and the per-session moment-of-use re-check at client.py:322-326 (pinned(exe, pin_sha256) -> SessionRefused) is silently skipped for every developer/reviewer session; the session result also loses its pinned_sha256 field (client.py:374). An attacker (or an accidental rebuild) who replaces the binary at the pinned path AFTER runspec/between sessions is caught in the shipped code by the first session's re-check (run stops, provenance preserved) but goes undetected under the mutant: the paid provider work runs on a non-pinned binary while RUN.json's rec["client_pin"] (run.py:537) and the runspec binary-sha256 still assert the pinned bytes were used — a false, silent client-provenance claim. This is exactly the TOCTOU the feature's own docstrings name ("re-checked at the moment of use (the OCR pattern)", run.py:529-530 / client.py:322); the re-check is the sole per-session defense and the mutant is its only guard. Exploit is direct: dropping the entry alone defeats the guarantee, needing only the ordinary swap threat the check exists for. Gap is REAL: the sole test (tests/v2/test_v22_client_pin_fence.py::test_the_pin_is_rechecked_at_the_moment_of_use, line 95) calls client.session(pin_sha256=...) directly, bypassing run.execute's kw build; no test drives client_pin through run.execute, so the mutant survives the suite. The proposed kill test (settings.client_pin set -> assert the session receives pin_sha256 == client_pin['sha256'] so pinned() fires; optionally a mid-run swap raises SessionRefused) is sound and absent. Downgrade proof attempted and failed: the value is an enforcement gate (not diagnostic), not dominated by any other per-session byte check, and not re-derived (kw is the only carrier). Calibrated to high, not critical: invariant_impact=none (not one of the nine RFC invariants nor the INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY owner invariant; client_pin is an OPTIONAL D4 feature), the product PASS/VERIFIED verdict on the code is untouched (only client-binary provenance is forged), and it is gated behind the opt-in pin plus an active mid-run file-swap precondition with a residual one-time pre-run/runspec check.

gaps.invariant_impact: §4 registry invariant 'an invariant without an enforcement mechanism is a documented intention, not an invariant' + runtime-arming attestation (RUNTIME_STATEMENT: 'every CODE enforcement mechanism resolved from the installed kernel'); loss touches every CODE mechanism, incl. I.approval-binds-both-hashes, II.harness-owned-probes/run_probe, IX.probe-api, all.invariant-error-is-base-exception
gaps.rationale: The CODE-resolution loop in register_runtime is the ONLY place at runtime that checks each invariant's CODE enforcement attribute actually imports and resolves (resolve() does importlib.import_module + per-part hasattr). The mutant makes the loop resolve STATIC_RULE mechanisms instead and skip CODE. The only other CODE touch, runtime_mechanism_digest, imports each module's file and digests its bytes but never accesses the named attribute, so a CODE enforcement function deleted or renamed while its module still imports is no longer caught: register_runtime/arm_runtime still succeed, require_armed passes, and run.py writes code_mechanism_digest + RUNTIME_STATEMENT into the run record falsely attesting that every CODE mechanism resolved — a silent false guarantee on the authority/arming + provenance path, re-derived as true by verify.py's oracle. Survives because on the dev tree the returned digests are unchanged (computed independently at the end) and all STATIC_RULE mechanisms load kernel_static_checks.py fine, so test_runtime_registration_agrees_with_the_full_one and test_a_registry_that_does_not_register_arms_nothing both pass. The mutant also secretly rebinds register_runtime to the tree-bound kernel_static_checks.py, contradicting its installed-kernel purpose.
gaps.kill_test_sketch: assertRaises(RegistrationError) when register_runtime is given a full I..IX registry in which one Invariant's CODE mechanism ref names a present module but a missing attribute (e.g. 'aisef2.product.approval:NO_SUCH_ATTR'); AND assert register_runtime still returns a RegisteredRuntime when a STATIC_RULE ref is broken but every CODE mechanism resolves (runtime registration must not resolve static rules).
gaps.verify_basis:
REAL gap, but downgraded from critical/direct to HIGH/indirect. register_runtime is run.py's first act on every run (arm_runtime -> RUN.json records RUNTIME_STATEMENT: 'every CODE enforcement mechanism resolved from the installed kernel'); it is the SOLE runtime fail-closed guard for that attestation. Original L449/L450 calls resolve(m) on each CODE mechanism, whose importlib.import_module + per-part hasattr catches a deleted/renamed enforcement qualname. The mutant resolves STATIC_RULE mechanisms instead and never checks any CODE attribute.

UPHOLD (why not benign/medium): construct/ship a kernel where one CODE enforcement attribute is deleted or renamed while its module still imports and is not hit on a given run's hot path (e.g. aisef2.product.contract:names_test_artefact for IX.probe-refuses-test-artefacts). Original arm_runtime raises RegistrationError -> run fails closed. Mutant: arm_runtime succeeds, run completes VERIFIED, RUN.json falsely attests every CODE mechanism resolved (provenance forgery on the authority/arming path) with the IX refusal silently absent. verify.py does NOT catch it: same kernel, its oracle re-derives the identical tampered-byte code_mechanism_digest (self-consistency only, nothing pins it to a frozen value); tampered kernel -> kernel_digest() differs (it hashes every aisef2 .py byte) so _invariant_problems skips the comparison and returns only a note (confirmed by test_an_absent_field...not_compared). The missing-attribute-but-importable case is thus genuinely observable and the proposed assertRaises(RegistrationError) kill test distinguishes mutant from original, so the mutant is not equivalent and the no-test-can-tell downgrade FAILS. Survival in-suite confirmed: no P0 test asserts missing-CODE-attribute fail-closed; the only RegistrationError assertion uses REGISTRY[1:]/[:-1], caught by the unmutated ids!=list(InvariantId) check; returned digests are recomputed at the end independent of the loop so all digest-equality tests still pass.

DOWNGRADE (why not critical/direct): no harm on the shipped/untampered kernel (mutant == original there). The defeat requires a SECOND, independent kernel-integrity defect — a CODE enforcement attribute missing from a still-importable module — which is the exact condition this guard exists to catch; it is not reachable via attacker-supplied run input, so exploit is indirect. Partial domination: a CODE module that fully FAILS TO IMPORT is still caught because register_runtime ends by calling runtime_mechanism_digest (importlib.import_module -> ImportError -> RegistrationError); and any CODE mechanism actively invoked on the hot path (require_approved, run_probe, fold, charge, classify, etc.) crashes at its call site if deleted, so the silent false-VERIFIED only materializes for a deletable-and-unexercised mechanism. The first-pass blast radius also overstates: all.invariant-error-is-base-exception is in UNCONTAINABLE, resolved by the UNMUTATED L452 CODE loop and re-asserted by the unmutated issubclass check at L454, so it is unaffected by this mutant. Net: a defense-in-depth fail-closed / provenance guard on the run control path is genuinely weakened for the attribute-missing tamper subset (HIGH), not an independently attacker-exploitable false PASS on normal inputs (not critical).

gaps.invariant_impact: Serve-surface tripwire guard DEVELOPER-CONFINEMENT-GAP-001, underpinning invariant III (developer-independence of the product proof: III.developer-tests-are-not-product-proof / III.confinement-from-env).
gaps.rationale: The `except ValueError: return True` is a DELIBERATE fail-closed (docstring: 'refuse rather than guess'). Returning None is falsy at the sole consumer `if _bundle_hit(...)` in scan_repo (run.py L593 then raises RunRefused), so marker-bearing text that does not parse as JSON (a truncated/corrupted project bundle, or prose quoting a marker) flips LEAK->CLEAN. No test feeds marker-bearing-but-invalid JSON, so the except arm is never asserted. HIGH: a stated fail-closed trust guard silently turned fail-open on the refusal path; for an all-UNSCANNED project (no needles) scan_text cannot compensate, so a non-independent proof can run and report PASS.
gaps.kill_test_sketch: assert tripwire._bundle_hit('aisef-v2-project/1 {this is not valid json', project) is True  # marker + unparseable JSON must be refused, not CLEAN
gaps.verify_basis: HOT RATING STANDS (uphold scenario is real; downgrade fails). Control path: _bundle_hit is consumed only at scan_repo L126 `if _bundle_hit(text, project): hits.append({...,"(the project bundle itself)"})`; scan_repo["hits"] gates run.py L593-594 `if rec["stimulus_tripwire"]["hits"]: raise RunRefused(...)`. None is falsy, so the mutant drops the bundle hit → no refusal. Concrete exploit: a project whose contracts are all UNSCANNED (stimuli <16 canonical chars — a real, test-covered class via test_a_contract_too_small_to_scan_is_named_unscanned) has wire["needles"]=={}, so scan_text can never produce a hit. Its own bundle/authoring doc (carrying the sealed stimulus/observable) is committed into the baseline tree the developer is served — precisely DEVELOPER-CONFINEMENT-GAP-001 ("the project's own bundle committed into the tree the developer reads"). The committed copy carries a marker but is not a single parseable JSON object (truncated/partial write, git conflict markers, trailing garbage, JSONL/multi-doc, markdown-wrapped authoring doc, or prose quoting the marker) → json.loads raises JSONDecodeError (ValueError) → the except arm. CORRECT code returns True → bundle hit → hits non-empty → RunRefused fires; developer-independence preserved. MUTANT returns None → no hit, and empty needles mean scan_text adds nothing → verdict CLEAN, hits==[] → no refusal → the run proceeds on a tree the developer reads that contains the sealed stimulus, and a non-developer-independent proof can run and report PASS/VERIFIED. Observable wrong outcome: a refusal that must fire does not; a false VERIFIED. This defeats invariant III (III.confinement-from-env / III.developer-tests-are-not-product-proof) via the serve-surface tripwire that underpins DEVELOPER-CONFINEMENT-GAP-001 — a stated fail-closed trust guard silently turned fail-open on its refusal path. DOWNGRADE REFUTED: the value is not re-derived (check_repository L229-250 only checks the baseline commit + requirements sha256, it does not scan the tree for a leaked bundle), not dominated (tripwire is the sole tree-bundle detector; for UNSCANNED projects scan_text provably contributes nothing), and not diagnostic (it drives RunRefused). Not an equivalent mutant: the sole consumer uses the result in a boolean `if`, where None and True take opposite branches. It survives only because no existing test feeds a marker-bearing-but-invalid-JSON text — both bundle tests feed valid JSON reaching the dict/format/ids path (L103-107), never the except arm. Proposed kill test is valid: tripwire._bundle_hit('aisef-v2-project/1 {this is not valid json', project) is True (marker + unparseable JSON must refuse, not CLEAN); an integration kill is scan_repo over a tree holding a truncated marker-bearing bundle for an all-UNSCANNED project → expect verdict LEAK.

gaps.invariant_impact: DEVELOPER-CONFINEMENT-GAP-001 serve-surface tripwire soundness for all composite (list/tuple/dict) stimulus/observable; not INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY

On the three refusal paths (scan_repo/RunRefused, client session/SessionRefused, OCR/CapabilityUnrunnable) this yields a SILENT false CLEAN: a structured stimulus/observable whose only distinguishing >=16-char needle is the composite form, leaked in normal JSON outside a recognizable bundle, reaches the developer undetected while the record still reports it scanned. Attempted exploit (wrong/unverified binary admitted and reaching delivery PASS) FAILS because every developer and reviewer session re-checks the same pin at the moment of use: run.py:656 puts pin_sha256 into kw whenever client_pin is set; ad.Developer (adapters.py:87-88) and ad.Reviewer (adapters.py:181-182) call client.session(..., **kw); client.py:322-326 runs pinned(exe, pin_sha256) and raises SessionRefused BEFORE ProcessRange.start() — i.e. before any provider request. So VI Immutable Provenance and III Independent Evidence are UPHELD, not defeated: the pinned-binary guarantee holds via the dominant session re-check. (1) Could not build an upholding scenario. registry_digest is a content-identity hash whose value is meaningful only by comparison. (2) Benign proof. The sole decision point, verify.py:_invariant_problems L111, is gated at L108 behind rec["kernel_digest"] == R.kernel_digest(). kernel_digest (run.py:93-100) hashes every aisef2/*.py byte INCLUDING registry.py. So when the gate passes, run and verifier share byte-identical registry.py → identical registry_digest() → recorded value (written by arm_runtime→register_runtime→registry_digest) == recomputed value, always; L112 can never fire. A mutation to registry_digest shifts the recording side and the recomputing side IDENTICALLY within one kernel build, so the equality outcome is invariant under it. Empirical confirmation of why it survived: the only two tests exercising it — p0/test_invariants_runtime.py VerifyRederives.test_a_faithful_record_re_derives_clean (self-referential: both operands use the same mutated function → still ([],[])) and test_a_forged_digest_is_a_problem_on_the_same_kernel (injects "0"*64, which any non-zero mutated digest still differs from → still flagged) — both PASS under either reading of the mutant.

Information loss is also independently shadowed. Reading (1): "uncontainable" is a constant label carrying no per-registry information → pure constant shift, zero discriminating power lost; even the proposed kill test (vary an UNCONTAINABLE id) can't distinguish it, since ids remain in the inner tuples — effectively equivalent. Reading (2): the dropped UNCONTAINABLE m.id values are still bound by mechanism_digest/runtime_mechanism_digest (_identity emits "{m.id} {m.ref} {sha}"), by render()/doc-drift (register(doc=True) refuses drift), and by kernel_digest (the id is literal source bytes) — any id change is a source change → kernel_digest change → caught.

confirmed_control_path=true in the literal sense: registry_digest's output does flow into verify's verdict-determining `problems` (verify.py 207-208 → 246 REFUTED/VERIFIED). But confirmed_exploit=none: the mutated value cannot flip that comparison on any reachable state, so it can produce no false PASS/VERIFIED, no authority expansion, no refusal bypass, and no provenance forgery that kernel_digest wouldn't independently catch. Not INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY-relevant. Severity: low.

gaps.invariant_impact: VI Immutable Provenance / V Reproducible Qualification (outer line delimiter of the digest input)
gaps.rationale: Joins the per-mechanism lines with '' instead of '\n' before the final sha256, so for any registry with more than one CODE mechanism the hashed bytes change and the inter-line boundary becomes implicit. This is the outermost canonical delimiter: without it, two different line-sets can concatenate to the same byte string (one line's trailing sha merging into the next line's id), so distinct registries can collide to one digest — provenance forgery / false match in verify. Runs on the normal path and changes the shipped digest, but no golden value pins it; a real collision needs crafted inputs, so indirect/high.
gaps.kill_test_sketch: golden digest for the default multi-mechanism registry, plus assert that registries whose flattened lines would concatenate identically under '' still differ under the real '\n' join.
gaps.verify_basis: Benign — the mutated delimiter can never produce a divergent observable, so it defeats no guarantee. The digest's only control-path consumer is verify.py:113 (inv["code_mechanism_digest"] != invariants.runtime_mechanism_digest() -> a problem that lowers the verdict to REFUTED, verify.py:207-208,246). That comparison is gated at verify.py:108 by rec["kernel_digest"] == R.kernel_digest(). kernel_digest() (run.py:93-100) hashes EVERY aisef2/**/*.py file LF-normalized; every CODE mechanism module and registry.py itself live under aisef2/, and runtime_mechanism_digest reads exactly those module bytes — a strict subset. So whenever the gate passes, registry.py is byte-identical on both sides (so the '\n'-vs-'' join used to WRITE the stored digest at run.py:516 equals the one used to RECOMPUTE it) and the hashed inputs are byte-identical too; stored == recomputed ALWAYS under either join. When kernel_digest differs, line 113 is never reached (early return, verify.py:109). The mechanism digest is thus strictly dominated by kernel_digest: a tautological internal-consistency check that cannot yield false PASS/VERIFIED, false REFUTED, authority expansion, or provenance forgery. The first-pass forgery/collision scenario is unreachable: verify.py:113 calls runtime_mechanism_digest() with the fixed default REGISTRY (no attacker-chosen registry), the per-line hex64 fields are sha256 of real imported-module bytes (not attacker-controlled), and a colliding kernel would first have to match the full-file, \0-delimited kernel_digest — if it matches the kernels are byte-identical (nothing to forge), if it differs the digest is never compared. It IS a genuine coverage gap (no golden literal pins the digest; test_invariants_runtime.py:27,36 compare runtime_mechanism_digest() to itself, so the mutant survives the suite), but no real execution path can distinguish '\n' from '', so the risk of the gap is low rather than high.

gaps.invariant_impact: VI Immutable Provenance (fail-closed CODE-mechanism resolution) + InvariantError uncontainability (aisef2/errors.py, RFC §4)
gaps.rationale: Drops AttributeError from the except tuple, so `.__file__` on a module that lacks it (e.g. a built-in like sys) propagates a raw, containable AttributeError instead of being converted to RegistrationError (a BaseException-derived, uncontainable InvariantError). This is the most reachable of the four drops through the public arming path: resolve() does not read __file__, so arm_runtime()/register_runtime() with a crafted CODE ref (ref='sys:...') reach it. A raw AttributeError can be swallowed by an `except Exception` boundary, turning a fail-closed registration into fail-open, whereas RegistrationError cannot be contained. Medium not high because the shipped run arms the frozen REGISTRY (never triggers this) behind run.py's `except BaseException` boundary, so defeating a guarantee needs a non-default registry plus a containing boundary.

The AttributeError branch is reachable only when a CODE mechanism's target module lacks __file__ entirely (a built-in); __file__=None gives TypeError and a missing file gives OSError, both still caught by the mutant. All 17 CODE targets in the frozen default REGISTRY are file-backed aisef2.* modules with usable __file__ (verified empirically; default runtime_mechanism_digest succeeds), so the branch is dead code for the shipped registry — the mutant is behaviorally identical there. Every production caller (run.py:516, verify.py:113, p3_evidence.py, freeze_conformance.py, q5.py, c2_p9.py, c2_k_nowork_001.py) calls arm_runtime()/runtime_mechanism_digest() with NO registry arg → the default frozen REGISTRY; only test code builds a non-default registry. The first-pass medium rested on "non-default registry + a containing except Exception boundary"; neither exists on a real path. Even the hypothetical crafted-registry call is wrapped in run.py by `except BaseException` (line 697), which catches RegistrationError and a raw AttributeError identically, records failure, and re-raises — so the two exception types are indistinguishable at the only production boundary around the arming call. Demonstrated: a crafted registry with ref 'sys:modules' makes the original raise RegistrationError (BaseException, not Exception) and the mutant escape a raw AttributeError (Exception), so the proposed kill test is valid and this is NOT an equivalent mutant at the unit level — but the behavior it covers is error-type/uncontainability hygiene for an input the frozen registry can never produce, behind a BaseException boundary. gaps.rationale: Drops ImportError, so importlib.import_module(target) failing propagates a raw, containable ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError instead of RegistrationError. Two real callers, neither yields a wrong observable. (1) Arming path run.py:516 arm_runtime -> register_runtime: register_runtime calls resolve(m) on every CODE mechanism (registry.py:448-453) BEFORE runtime_mechanism_digest (L456). resolve already imports each target and converts ImportError->RegistrationError (L220-223), caching the module in sys.modules, so the second import_module inside runtime_mechanism_digest returns the cached object and cannot raise ImportError. The ImportError branch is dead on the arming path; the mutant is unobservable there, record digests unchanged, no false PASS. (2) Verify path verify.py:_invariant_problems:113 calls runtime_mechanism_digest() DIRECTLY (not via resolve) — the caller the first-pass under-weighted. But it is gated at L108 on rec.kernel_digest == R.kernel_digest(), and kernel_digest() (run.py:93-100) hashes every .py of the installed aisef2 package by path+bytes, so a match means every first-party REGISTRY CODE module file is present and byte-identical — an ImportError is near-unreachable (would need an environmental missing third-party import). The proposed kill test (direct call asserting RegistrationError not ImportError) can distinguish the exception type, so this is a genuine test-coverage gap on a defensive fail-closed branch — real, but benign. confirmed_control_path=true (function is on verify's and run's control paths; the mutated except handler is live), confirmed_exploit=none (no concrete scenario yields a wrong accept/forgery).

The ORDER of the `hits` list inside journaled RUN.json — present ONLY when a leak was found, i.e. on a run that is being REFUSED (RunRefused). json.dumps uses sort_keys=True which sorts dict keys, not list elements, so the hits order is preserved as-is. gaps.invariant_impact: evidence-anchor reproducibility (run.py _content_sha: "a re-serialised identical record is the same record"; related VI.record-digest, V.comparable) — the returned list ordering is serialized into the sealed RUN.json content hash
gaps.rationale: list(set(dropped)) returns the dropped diagnostics in CPython hash order (string hash is PYTHONHASHSEED-randomized across kernel processes) instead of stable alphabetical order. The set contents are identical, so leak detection and the verdict are unchanged — the tripwire still refuses a real leak. But `dropped` is returned verbatim, copied unsorted into scan_repo's report (run.py: "dropped": list(wire['dropped'])), stored in rec['stimulus_tripwire'], and written to RUN.json. RUN.json is content-hashed into the evidence manifest/anchor via _content_sha, and sort_keys=True sorts dict keys but NOT list elements — so two runs of identical frozen inputs with >=2 dropped contracts produce different anchors, breaking the reproducible-anchor property. It fails toward a spurious mismatch (not a false PASS), so exploitability is indirect, not direct. No current test constrains order: the dropped test only asserts any(d.startswith('BC-ADD:')).
gaps.kill_test_sketch: Build a project whose public text collides with needles from >=2 contracts so len(wire['dropped'])>=2, then assert wire['dropped'] == sorted(wire['dropped']); strengthen with a determinism check that needles_of produces the identical dropped list under two subprocess runs with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and PYTHONHASHSEED=1.
gaps.verify_basis: BENIGN. The mutated value (order of the `dropped` diagnostic list) reaches no control decision and no identity-sealing hash. (1) Security: `scan_repo` verdict = `"LEAK" if hits else "CLEAN"` and `refusal()` route on `hits` only, never on `dropped`; the mutant keeps `set(dropped)` identical (both original and mutant dedupe the same set), so needles/hits/verdict/refusal are identical — no false CLEAN, no refusal bypass, no authority expansion. (2) Identity: runspec_hash (V.runspec-hash) is built by runspec_of/layers_of, which never reference wire/stimulus_tripwire; record_digest (VI.record-digest) and semantic_hash likewise exclude the tripwire output — so "same frozen inputs give same run identity" is untouched. The only hash that includes the order is the per-run evidence anchor via _content_sha(RUN.json), but the anchor is a per-directory integrity binding, computed once (run.py:727 writes RUN.json with sort_keys=True which does NOT sort list elements, then EVIDENCE.json binds it) and re-derived by verify() from the SAME on-disk file (evidence_manifest reads files, never re-runs the tripwire) → stored==fresh always holds within a run. (3) The first-pass "reproducible-anchor property" across independent runs is not a real guarantee: two runs already differ (started timestamp, journal, session streams, model output) so anchors differ by design, and verify.py explicitly notes the anchor "does not prove the run happened as its journal says." Reseal/freeze_manifest re-hash existing bytes, so a historical RUN.json retains its original order regardless of the mutant. No test constrains dropped order (test_v22_tripwire only asserts `any(d.startswith('BC-ADD:'))` or `dropped==[]`), and no real path compares two independently-generated dropped lists — so the survivor is genuine coverage but benign ordering hygiene, defeating no guarantee. Downgraded medium->low; exploitability none, not indirect; the mutated value is off the control path.

gaps.invariant_impact: evidence-anchor reproducibility (run.py _content_sha; related VI.record-digest, V.comparable) — the returned unscanned list ordering is serialized into the sealed RUN.json content hash
gaps.rationale: list(set(unscanned)) returns the unscanned contract ids in hash order (PYTHONHASHSEED-randomized) rather than sorted order. The set of ids is unchanged, so no contract is silently covered or dropped and the verdict is unaffected. But the list is returned verbatim, passed unsorted through scan_repo ("unscanned": list(wire['unscanned'])), stored in rec['stimulus_tripwire'] and written to RUN.json, whose canonical JSON (sort_keys=True does not reorder list elements) is the content hash feeding the evidence anchor. With >=2 unscanned contracts, identical frozen inputs yield different anchors across runs — a reproducibility regression that fails toward a spurious mismatch, hence indirect exploitability. The existing test asserts unscanned == ['BC-ADD'] with a single element, so order is never constrained.
gaps.kill_test_sketch: Construct a project with >=2 contracts whose stimulus/observable are all under MIN_NEEDLE so len(wire['unscanned'])>=2, then assert wire['unscanned'] == sorted(wire['unscanned']); add a cross-PYTHONHASHSEED subprocess determinism assertion that the list is byte-identical.
gaps.verify_basis: BENIGN — downgrade from medium to low. (1) Not on any control path: the tripwire's only decision inputs are `hits` (run.py:593 refusal) and `wire["needles"]` (sessions scan in client.py:328 / adapters.py:240); `scan_repo` computes verdict as "LEAK" if hits else "CLEAN", with hits sourced only from `_bundle_hit` and `scan_text(..., needles)`. `unscanned` (like `dropped`) is read by NO refusal/admission/verdict/authority anywhere in aisef2 — it is pure diagnostic text recorded so the operator sees which short-stimulus contracts are tripwire-blind. (2) No within-run anchor defeat: verify() reads RUN.json from disk and recomputes evidence_manifest from the SAME on-disk files; `_content_sha` re-serialises the identical bytes, so the list order written equals the order re-hashed; the anchor is compared only to expect_anchor, the value THIS run printed. verify never re-derives needles_of/scan_repo. So the mutant produces no manifest/anchor mismatch, no false PASS/VERIFIED, no forgery, no journal mismatch. (3) No cross-run reproducibility guarantee exists to break: RUN.json carries `started` (clock), usage, journal digests and diagnostics, making its content hash inherently run-unique; no check compares anchors across independent runs of identical inputs. `_content_sha`'s 'reproducibility' is stability under re-serialisation of the identical record, which the mutant does not affect. The lineage predecessor anchor is recorded, not recomputed-and-matched. (4) The cited invariants are unrelated: V.comparable (runspec) compares RunSpec capability tuples/grades; VI.record-digest seals ProbeRecord fields; neither touches the tripwire unscanned list. The genuine sort-for-determinism invariant WITH a kill test is preflight.fingerprint_fields (tests/v2/test_s2_kills.py L943-954), whose value is actually re-derived and matched — unlike unscanned. The first-pass conflated a within-run tamper-evidence anchor with a nonexistent cross-run reproducibility comparator. Existing tests (test_v22_tripwire.py L51 asserts unscanned==['BC-ADD'], single element; L39 asserts []) never constrain order for >=2 elements, so the mutant genuinely survives — a real coverage gap, but it defeats no guarantee. Sorting is worthwhile house determinism hygiene (add one direct assertion on needles_of output order / a PYTHONHASHSEED subprocess check), not a security or integrity fix; no test on any real downstream path can distinguish the mutant, which is why the proposed kill test must be a new synthetic assertion on the function's output ordering.
